A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Q-Eval-100K/Q-Eval-Score study, including four supplementary pages. Text and rendered pages 3–15 are identical; differences on pages 1–2 concern formatting and version labeling. The material supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-rating analyses, benchmark evaluations, ablations and cross-dataset results, including Tables 2–6 and supplementary Table 8.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original human-rating analyses and experimental results in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct backbone, context prompts, CE/MSE losses, score aggregation and Vague-to-Specific inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 100K image/video dataset, long-prompt subset, GenAI-Bench evaluation and supplementary AGIQA, T2VQA and TIFA160 evaluations.

E2.justification: The comparator sets and default-weight versus trained variants match within every corresponding comparison in Tables 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8.

E3.justification: The 80:20 split, one-frame-per-second video sampling, one-epoch training, 5,000-instance long-prompt evaluation and instance/model-level SRCC and PLCC protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain identical SFT, context-prompt and loss ablations in Table 4, Vague-to-Specific testing in Table 5, annotation-distribution analyses and supplementary comparison examples in Figure 8.

E5.justification: Annotation counts and score-variance reporting, including supplementary Figure 9, are identical. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including supplementary results. For example, Q-Eval-Score image instance-level SRCC remains 0.732 for quality in Table 2 and 0.822 for alignment in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain identical rating mappings, scoring definitions, losses and prompt-combination mathematics. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about dataset scale, separate quality/alignment scoring, long-prompt handling and generalization.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are identical, including temporal-information loss from frame sampling and the subjectivity, scalability and potential biases of human annotations.

D1.justification: Training hardware, implementation details, supplementary prompt instructions and stated release plans are unchanged. The existing repository address becomes clickable, but its destination and access information remain the same.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and all 77 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv version/date label changes from v1, 4 March 2025, to v3, 15 June 2025. Prose, terminology, section order and supplementary organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract’s repository URL changes to a colored monospaced hyperlink and wraps onto another line, causing limited text reflow across pages 1–2. Figures, tables and subsequent page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The complete scientific content, evidence, limitations and reproducibility disclosures are unchanged, including the supplementary material. The clickable link offers a small navigation convenience, but the formatting and version-label updates do not materially change overall paper quality.
